To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed a system, called VisReduce, that can incrementally compute information visualizations from large datasets in a distributed, fault-tolerant manner, and that VisReduce is faster than three other popular data systems, namely PostgreSQL, Clouder Impala, and Apache Hive.
our method is significantly faster (up to 100x faster) than other methods and is guaranteed to respond within 1 second.
our method is able to produce visualizations faster and more responsively, even for large, long-running MapReduce jobs, than the other systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to efficiently construct visualizations of large data sets, and how to do so in a way that is responsive to the user.
how to build visualizations in a fast and responsive way for exploratory analysis of large datasets.
the design of efficient algorithms for visualizing large datasets in a responsive manner, and the implementation of such algorithms in a distributed, parallel environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system is the only one that can guarantee end-user responsiveness for all the queries we ran.
VisReduce provides a significant improvement in performance and responsiveness of visualizations of large datasets.
VisReduce provides a significant speedup in visualization generation, especially for long-running queries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VisReduce is a fast and responsive incremental information system for exploratory data visualization of large datasets.
our approach is able to build visualizations of data sets that are 1000 times larger than those of the best alternative, in less time and with guaranteed end-user responsiveness.
VisReduce is the first system to provide fast, interactive visual analytics of large datasets in a distributed setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of a compressed columnar store and a MapReduce-style algorithm allows for fast and responsive visualization of large datasets, even when using a single commodity server with a single CPU core.

a combination of MapReduce and compressed columnar data stores can provide a significant performance improvement over existing systems, while maintaining the flexibility and scalability of a data warehouse system.
a MapReduce-based algorithm can provide significant performance and responsiveness benefits when compared to a relational database, data warehouse or MapReduce-based data store.
